newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - February 27.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - February 27.

text.p: The following were the leading stories in the Sri Lankan press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
Intervention by Sri Lanka High Commission and other groups leads to cancellation of a symposium sponsored by the Tamil Eelam Economic Development Organisation at London's Imperial College.
Police investigate complaint by Gamini Athukorale, opposition United National Party (UNP) general secretary that unknown gunmen shot at him near Ratnapura in central Sri Lanka on Wednesday.

Susantha Punchinilame, a suspect in the killing of a ruling coalition lawmaker, to be produced in a Colombo court on Friday in connection with abduction and killing of three youths in 1980s. Punchinilame was out on bail at the time of the Ellawala shooting on February 11.
UNP leader Ranil Wickremesinghe says his party's government did not keep records on about 5,000 firearms issued to political parties in 1980s.
Elections Commissioner to accept four lists of names rejected when nominations closed for March 21 local government polls.
Police deploy special groups of officers to curb violence ahead of March 21 polls.
Retail price of seven essential items of food reduced at state-owned co-operative shops.
